transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to begin our routine check-in for the restored silent film 'The Last Harbor' before we lock the final presentation package. As it stands, the draft proposes digital projection, a live string trio, and the standard 16:9 screen mask. I'd like to hear from each of you on the archive, music, and technical aspects so we can make sure everything is in order before I make my binding decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important archive-license amendment I received yesterday. It confirms that this festival screening of 'The Last Harbor' must use the Northlight Archive's 35mm print — not digital projection. It also requires retaining the film's original 1.33:1 image framing without cropping, which conflicts with the proposed standard 16:9 screen mask. Additionally, we must display the exact credit 'Restored by Northlight Archive.' I haven't entered this amendment into the festival rights tracker yet, but it's binding on our presentation package.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important technical finding from this morning. I tested the screening room with the live-score setup and confirmed that the room's pit and monitoring arrangement supports only a solo piano, not the proposed string trio. Additionally, the commissioned score cleared for this performance is 'Tide Marks,' and I have not yet updated the technical run sheet to reflect any of this.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for these critical findings. Let me make sure I understand the full picture before I settle the package. Julian, you've told me the archive-license amendment requires: 35mm print instead of digital projection, original 1.33:1 framing without cropping, and the exact credit 'Restored by Northlight Archive.' Nia, you've told me the screening room pit and monitoring only supports a solo piano — not the string trio — and that the commissioned score cleared for this performance is 'Tide Marks.' Both of you have also noted that you haven't yet updated your respective trackers or run sheets. Before I make my binding decision, I want to confirm: are there any other archive, music, or technical considerations I should be aware of? If not, I'm prepared to settle the final package now, incorporating all of these requirements.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: From the archive side, there are no other considerations beyond what I've already shared. The three requirements from the amendment — 35mm print, 1.33:1 framing without cropping, and the exact credit 'Restored by Northlight Archive' — are the complete set of archive and rights obligations I'm aware of for this screening. I'll enter the amendment into the festival rights tracker as soon as we conclude this check-in.
